content.text:
Redesign the entire MarginGhost frontend into one cohesive premium financial-intelligence interface with fully functional Light and Dark modes.

PROJECT
- Next.js 16.4, React, TypeScript
- Repository: D:\Aristo
- Current design branch: ui-redesign
- Existing redesigned homepage uses mg-home classes in src/app/page.tsx and src/app/globals.css.
- The homepage currently uses a dark emerald aesthetic.
- Investigation, synthetic demo, evaluation, and Judge Preview pages still use the older light theme.

OBJECTIVE

Unify every frontend page under the same visual design language as the new dark homepage and MarginGhost launch poster.

The application should feel like a premium financial investigation platform, with excellent readability, accessibility, and professional visual hierarchy.

Do not sacrifice functionality for visual effects.

DESIGN SYSTEM

DARK THEME — DEFAULT
Background: #08120E
Card surfaces: #101C18 / #15241E
Primary text: #F5F7F2
Secondary text: #A2B2A9
Accent: #B5F0BD
Emerald: #184F3B
Borders: subtle green-gray

LIGHT THEME
Background: #F7F8F4
Card surfaces: #FFFFFF
Primary text: #20342B
Secondary text: #61736A
Accent: #184F3B
Borders: #D8E1D9

Use design tokens through CSS variables. Avoid duplicating entire stylesheets for each theme.

THEME SWITCHER

Implement a real global Light / Dark toggle.

Requirements:
- Dark mode by default for a first-time visitor.
- User-selected preference persists through localStorage.
- Apply the theme consistently across all application routes.
- Avoid hydration mismatches or visible theme flashes.
- Accessible toggle with descriptive labels and keyboard support.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
- Make light mode equally polished and readable.
- Do not introduce a large theme library unless necessary.
- Ensure the toggle is present in the shared navigation.

PAGES TO REDESIGN

1. HOMEPAGE (/)

Preserve the newly redesigned homepage.

Refine its spacing, typography, responsive layout, and theme support.

Keep the static synthetic ₹18,000 showcase.

The hero should remain dramatic and premium.

2. INVESTIGATION (/investigate)

This is the primary product workspace.

Redesign:
- Header and navigation
- Hero/intro section
- Document upload cards
- Contract, purchase-order, invoice and amendment sections
- Document ID fields
- PDF extraction indicators
- Investigation progress/status panel
- Loading and error states
- Self-audit summary
- Findings and source-evidence presentation
- Printable report controls

Use a professional control-room layout with sophisticated card surfaces and clear visual states.

Keep dense financial evidence highly readable.

3. SYNTHETIC DEMO (/demo)

Redesign all three scenario cards:
- Potential overcharge
- Conflicting amendment
- Revised purchase order

Preserve exact dispositions and synthetic-only labeling.

Improve scenario selection, financial comparison, evidence navigation, and result readability.

Do not introduce real inference into synthetic demo mode.

4. EVALUATION (/evaluation)

Redesign the deterministic reliability dashboard.

Prominently show:
- Nine expected outcomes observed
- Nine deterministic scenarios passed
- Eight unsupported claims safely withheld

Retain explicit language that these are deterministic regression cases, not an AI model accuracy benchmark.

Improve scenario cards, PASS indicators, hierarchy, and information density.

5. JUDGE PREVIEW (/judge-preview)

Redesign:
- Password entry screen
- Unavailable/disabled state
- Loading and error messages
- Signed-in navigation
- Logout controls

Keep all authentication semantics unchanged.

Do not expose environment variables, credentials, or debug data.

6. REPORT AND PRINT

Create a professional evidence-first report matching the new product identity.

The in-browser report should respect the selected app theme.

The printed PDF report must always use a crisp white background with dark text, regardless of application theme.

Preserve:
- Exact source citations
- Financial calculations
- SUPPORTED / NEEDS REVIEW / REJECTED distinctions
- Five-check self-audit presentation
- Human-review disclaimers
- Current print functionality

Avoid almost-empty trailing PDF pages where possible without hiding any information.

SHARED COMPONENTS

Refactor duplicated navigation and visual components where appropriate:
- Logo
- Navigation
- Theme switch
- Buttons
- Cards
- Status badges
- Page headers
- Empty states
- Error states

Make all screens feel like one application.

RESPONSIVE DESIGN

Test at:
- 1440px desktop
- 1024px laptop/tablet
- 768px tablet
- 390px mobile

Ensure:
- No horizontal overflow
- Accessible buttons and inputs
- Readable evidence citations
- Usable document upload controls
- Consistent navigation

SECURITY AND FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS

Do not change:
- PDF extraction implementation
- Groq inference behavior
- Upstash Redis quotas
- Judge Preview authentication
- Session cookies
- CSRF protections
- Bounded request bodies
- Production API guards
- Evidence verification rules
- Deterministic arithmetic
- neatlogs instrumentation
- Entire integration
- Existing API contracts

The redesign is PRESENTATION ONLY.

Never expose live PDF upload forms to unauthorized production users.

Do not fabricate AI findings or replace functional workflows with mock interfaces.

TEST COVERAGE

Update tests/routes.test.ts to reflect the redesigned homepage.

The old assertion expects:
"Find invoice discrepancies"

Replace it with assertions for:
- "Know what every invoice should cost."
- Public synthetic demo link
- Evaluation link
- Restricted live investigation messaging

Add useful tests for theme functionality and shared navigation.

Do not weaken existing security tests or remove legitimate assertions.

WORKFLOW

First inspect the existing layout, global CSS, pages, and home-client component.

Provide a concise implementation plan identifying the shared theme system and route dependencies.

Then implement the redesign in manageable phases:
A. Global theme tokens and shared navigation
B. Investigation workspace
C. Synthetic demo
D. Evaluation
E. Judge Preview
F. Report and print CSS
G. Responsive and accessibility polish

Run:
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run lint
npm run build

If Linux dependencies prevent test/build execution, report that and leave complete verification for Windows.

Do not modify .env.
Do not commit, push, merge, or deploy.
Do not touch unrelated local files.

Report changed files, completed screens, known limitations, and verification results.
I’ll first map the app shell, route components, styles, and existing tests, then share a concise plan before editing. I’ll keep the work presentation-only and avoid unrelated files or `.env`.

content.text: Plan: the homepage already has its own `mg-home` visual system, while investigation/demo share `HomeClient` and report components; evaluation and Judge Preview are separate server/client routes. I’ll add one token-based theme layer and shared navigation/toggle, then update those route shells and component styles while preserving their existing workflow logic. I’ll also make the pre-hydration theme choice localStorage-aware to avoid a first-paint flash, and set report print colors independently of the selected theme.

content.text:
Implemented the presentation redesign across the homepage, investigation workspace, synthetic demo, evaluation, Judge Preview, and report views.

- Added a shared navigation and accessible Light/Dark toggle. Dark is the first-visit default; the choice persists in `localStorage` and is applied before page rendering.
- Added theme tokens and route styles, including white-background print styling for reports.
- Updated evaluation labels and route tests. Existing workflow logic, authentication checks, and API behavior were left unchanged.

**Verification:** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `git diff --check` passed. `npm test` could not complete because this Linux environment has Windows-only `esbuild` binaries; `npm run build` could not run because Linux Next.js native bindings are missing. Per your instruction, complete test/build verification remains for Windows. I also could not visually inspect the requested viewport sizes in a browser.

Changed files include [globals.css](/mnt/d/Aristo/src/app/globals.css), [navigation.tsx](/mnt/d/Aristo/src/app/navigation.tsx), [theme-switch.tsx](/mnt/d/Aristo/src/app/theme-switch.tsx), [home-client.tsx](/mnt/d/Aristo/src/app/home-client.tsx), [evaluation/page.tsx](/mnt/d/Aristo/src/app/evaluation/page.tsx), [judge-preview-client.tsx](/mnt/d/Aristo/src/app/judge-preview/judge-preview-client.tsx), [layout.tsx](/mnt/d/Aristo/src/app/layout.tsx), [page.tsx](/mnt/d/Aristo/src/app/page.tsx), and [routes.test.ts](/mnt/d/Aristo/tests/routes.test.ts). No commit, push, or deployment was performed.
